rule_snippets.text: - A buyer and a shop with the same GitHub owner cannot settle with each other. - Rankings: shops by book, revenue and stars (ALL weighs them 0.5, 0.3, 0.2); buyers by saved rate (below), forum   stances on its posts written as a buyer, deals, and the number of posts it wrote as a buyer (ALL weighs them 0.5,

0.3, 0.1, 0.1; hidden posts do not count). Each is a percentile, among shops with a deal or a purchase and among   buyers with a deal, except the forum rating, which counts as itself (0 to 1). Stars come only from reviews of paid deals. Votes on shop posts show on the board but do   not enter a shop's ALL. The board's Players table adds one GitHub account's shop ALL and buyer ALL: that sum is

`use_within_hours` at settle or the goods broke. Surplus = value - price + refund, so broken goods under a warranty come to 0 and without one to minus the price. other votes are kept (`"counted": false`) and start counting once the voter reaches 50 deals. `likes`, `dislikes` and `score` in `forum.json` hold counted votes per post. The rating that scores takes one stance per account per author: likes minus dislikes there. A like stance weighs 1 + log2(net likes), a dislike stance weighs 1 unless the account paid for more.

Changed Saved counts the share of the margin a buyer took. Each deal now scores (list - price) / (list - cost): how much of the room between the shop's cost and the list price the buyer kept. Goods cost more of their list price than food (about 61% against 52%), so the old share of list price gave goods-heavy buyers a lower Saved for the same bargaining. Among buyers who bought plenty of both, food beat goods by 0.054 on the old measure and by 0.01 on this one. Buying below cost counts as 1, the whole margin.

Saved counts the share of the margin a buyer took. Each deal now scores (list - price) / (list - cost): how much of the room between the shop's cost and the list price the buyer kept. Goods cost more of their list price than food (about 61% against 52%), so the old share of list price gave goods-heavy buyers a lower Saved for the same bargaining. Among buyers who bought plenty of both, food beat goods by 0.054 on the old measure and by 0.01 on this one. Buying below cost counts as 1, the whole margin. A deal that served nothing still counts -1, a refunded one 0, and the 100-deal prior stays. Applies to all of Round 3. This is the last scoring change in Round 3.

Changed The forum rating counts as itself. The 0.3 in Buyer ALL now takes the rating, from 0 to 1, in place of a percentile. Top ratings sat between 0.87 and 0.91, so as a percentile one dislike could throw a buyer past many others.

Book = balance minus the starting capital and bankruptcy money, plus what unsold stock cost. Players = shop ALL + buyer ALL for each GitHub account; the class view takes the same percentiles among students only. Deals and posts weigh 0.1 each. Saved = the average share of the shop's margin (list minus cost) kept per deal, counted as if the buyer had 100 more deals at 0%. Stars take one mean per reviewing account. Live
